mbm-2026.clue: I count the red doors from the water.
mbm-2026.quote: From my kayak, three red boathouse doors look the same. The middle one has a little tin rooster on the roof. I hold my paddle straight up and give him my best salute.

mbm-2027.clue: I like the first light after the movie.
mbm-2027.quote: At afternoon shows we come out blinking. My sister closes one eye in the credits so she's ready for daylight. We took a photo after the last matinee and both of us are winking.

mbm-2028.clue: Two strokes for the ducks, one for me.
mbm-2028.quote: We painted a family of thumb-sized ducks on our canoe. My daughter kept count of the real ones that overtook us. Our painted ducks all tied for last place.

mbm-2029.clue: We thank the broom at the end, too.
mbm-2029.quote: After martial arts class I swept the mat with our instructor. He bowed to his reflection and the broom fell over with a thump. Now I hold it steady for the very last bow.

mbm-2030.clue: Look for the patch of blueberries beside the boot.
mbm-2030.quote: I drew my uncle a map of our hike and used my muddy boot for the mountain's outline. The marks in the heel made a surprisingly accurate blueberry patch.

mbm-2031.clue: The whistle comes from the wrong end of the bench.
mbm-2031.quote: I learned a sparrow's call by listening underneath our park bench. The old woman at the other end could whistle it, too. For ten minutes the actual sparrow watched us from the tree.

mbm-2032.clue: I bring the map closer when it snows.
mbm-2032.quote: I draw a little route in pencil between my radio and each new friend's town. During the snowstorm the lines got so thick around the valley I shaded them into a warm gray scarf.

mbm-2033.clue: My scissors leave room for the whiskers.
mbm-2033.quote: I cut a red paper cat for my aunt's front window. The paper between the whiskers was so thin she said the whole cat could feel a breeze. It twitches a little when the door opens.

mbm-2034.clue: I keep the note warm in the spoon drawer.
mbm-2034.quote: The choir gives me the low start to our favorite song. I practice it while I lay the breakfast table and the silverware rattles the tiniest bit. That is my smallest audience.

mbm-2035.clue: Gran gets the last tile and the last biscuit.
mbm-2035.quote: My grandmother balances a domino on its edge when she's deciding where to play. I once held my breath so long the kettle boiled twice. She took both the round and the last biscuit.

mbm-2036.clue: I remember the rally by its shadow.
mbm-2036.quote: At sunset our four shadows stretched across the beach court. I saw my partner's hand lift on the sand before I saw the actual hand. I set the ball there and she hit her cleanest winner.

mbm-2037.clue: The little silver spoon came home with me.
mbm-2037.quote: I didn't win the cobbler contest, but the woman next to me lent me her lucky spoon. We shared the last cherry. She gave me the spoon when I told her it was a better prize.

mbm-2038.clue: I can hear that ball with my eyes shut.
mbm-2038.quote: My first bowling ball has one small nick. It gives a little tick at the same spot every roll. Mum says it's like hearing my footsteps come home.

mbm-2039.clue: My favorite canoe photograph is mostly grass.
mbm-2039.quote: We landed on the wrong side of the island for lunch. My friend set the camera in a clump of grass. In the photo there are just two grinning faces and a canoe prow above the blades.

mbm-2040.clue: My sister names my climbing routes after soup.
mbm-2040.quote: At the climbing wall I got stuck under a hold the color of tomato soup. My sister called for a spoon. I reached it from the side and we went out for lunch to celebrate.

mbm-2041.clue: I stamp the inside corner first.
mbm-2041.quote: I made Mum a leather glasses case with a tiny fox inside the flap. She opens it slowly so the fox can look round before she takes the glasses out.

mbm-2042.clue: I brought the wrong sort of binoculars.
mbm-2042.quote: My nephew gave me two paper tubes tied with string for our bird walk. I spotted a kingfisher through them while he was still turning the focus wheel on mine. We called it a draw.

mbm-2043.clue: The lid grew its own chimney.
mbm-2043.quote: I built a butter crock that looked like our cottage. The little chimney is just right for a sprig of parsley. Dad won't start lunch till there's green smoke coming out.

mbm-2044.clue: Our postcard has a real corner missing.
mbm-2044.quote: I took my aunt to find the view on her old postcard. The building that used to fill its torn corner was gone and a pear tree was growing there. We bought two pears for the picture.

mbm-2045.clue: I put the bridge right on the crease.
mbm-2045.quote: I tooled a little river into a leather wallet and stamped a bridge across the fold. When my brother opens it, the bridge opens too. He flicks boats through with his thumb.

mbm-2046.clue: We tacked the set list inside the drum.
mbm-2046.quote: I kept knocking the paper off my music stand. Our drummer taped it to the clear head of her spare drum. Every time I glanced down the song bounced a little.

mbm-2047.clue: I let the first stone land twice.
mbm-2047.quote: Mum taught me baduk at a table with a hollow drawer. Each stone made an echo. We moved the board years ago and she still taps her finger for the second click.

mbm-2048.clue: The ocean scene tasted like lemon.
mbm-2048.quote: My grandfather always brought lemon sweets to the cinema. At the sound of the first wave he'd slip me one. I saw the same film again last week and bought a whole paper bag.

mbm-2049.clue: I traded my fair prize for a photograph.
mbm-2049.quote: I won a stuffed plum in the pastry contest. A little girl wanted it and her dad had a camera, so we swapped. In the picture all three of us are purple round the mouth.

mbm-2050.clue: I give our queens a window seat.
mbm-2050.quote: On windy days the park chess club moves into the greenhouse. We set both wooden queens beside the glass after the game. They look like two old friends watching the tomatoes grow.
